messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 5xx spike on /v1/generate from prod-us-east-1 after deploy 2026-03-15T14:12Z. Affected route: text-generation. Errors: 502/timeout. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

sasha: seeing it in dashboards, latency up ~3x and error rate ~12% on p99. A few customers hit. rolling back in progress?

chen: I deployed the small routing change (release/2026-03-15-release-c) 10m ago. It toggles model-routing FF 'exp_quant_routing' for 10% traffic.

ana: customers reported garbled token streams + 502s — likely model variant mismatch. quick check: some requests are going to quantized-ggml-v2 which doesn't support the new kv-cache layout we shipped.

mike: oncall here. can we flip the flag to 0? who has access to the FF service?

sasha: I can. Doing kill-switch now. /ff toggle exp_quant_routing 0 

incident-bot: action logged: user=sasha, action=toggle_flag, flag=exp_quant_routing, from=10% to=0%, time=1762504384

chen: flag flipped. traffic back to stable model-routing. watching metrics...

ana: errors dropped fast but some customers still seeing 502s from prior routed sessions. Need to invalidate kv-cache or restart sessions.

mike: what's impact surface? which customers? sales-liaison, please gather customer list so we can triage SLA exposure.

sales-liaison: pinged top 3 affected accounts via DM and asked for logs; I have enterprise-42 and client-omega on the hit list. ETA for response: 10m.

sasha: propose a minimal hotpatch: revert the single routing commit (sha: ab12c3f) from release branch and patch config to avoid auto-routing to quantized variant until we ship proper kv-cache support. Can someone prepare a PR?

chen: I can open revert PR now: git revert --no-commit ab12c3f && git commit -m "revert: temporary rollback of routing experiment due to kv-cache mismatch". Will push to hotfix/revert-exp-routing and ask CI to build.

ana: also we should restart affected pods for active sessions: kubectl rollout restart deployment/llm-runtime -n prod-us-east-1 --selector=zone=us-east-1-canary. That will evict stale sessions. Do it after PR lands.

mike: i'm pairing with chen. oncall-next @oncall-next are you ready to take handoff after I patch? I'll do a 15m sync before stepping out.

oncall-next: ready, be available for 30m. prefer if we document rollback steps in runbook quickly.

chen: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pull/4223 (revert ab12c3f). CI passed on draft. merging to hotfix branch after approvals.

incident-bot: [DEPLOY] hotfix/hf-4223 promoted to canary at 1762504800 by chen.

ana: canary metrics look good for 5min. error rate back to baseline on canary nodes. proceeding to full rollout.

mike: live rollout to prod starting. Command: ci promote hotfix/hf-4223 --env prod --safeguard=5m

sasha: rolling restarts queued. monitoring: token-level error traces show residual 500s from sessions started during the initial 10m window. we'll need to surface a remediation for affected customers: session-resubmit or temporary traffic pin to stable per-tenant.

sales-liaison: enterprise-42 confirmed decreased failures after flag flip and hotfix; they want a written incident note and confirmation when full rollback done.

mike: full rollout complete at 1762505102. post-rollout checks: p95 latency normal, error rate <0.5%.

ana: follow-up steps: 1) block exp_quant_routing in FF service until kv-cache patch lands (done), 2) schedule an infra patch to add compatibility shim for quantized-ggml, 3) run canary test harness for km-cache layout changes.

chen: created follow-up ticket INF-1187 for kv-cache compat; assigned to eng-runtime. Also PR to add defensive checks to routing logic to prevent routing to incompatible variants.

mike: handoff to oncall-next at 1762505260. oncall-next will monitor for 2 hours and escalate if regressions >1% error.

oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll watch the dashboards and patch the incident card with notes.

incident-bot: incident closed to active responders at 1762505345. severity: sev2 -> mitigated. Contact: support@redwood for customer follow-ups.

mike: quick postmortem notes in #postmortems please: root cause = feature flag allowed 10% traffic to an incompatible model variant; regression in kv-cache format landed earlier and wasn't flagged in canary; mitigation = FF kill-switch, revert single commit, hotfix rollout, pod restarts.

sasha: will draft the customer-facing postmortem and include timeline and next steps.

chen: tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for follow-ups.

sales-liaison: customers updated. no SLA credits requested yet; continuing to monitor.

ana: adding snippet to runbook: when model-routing causes 5xx spike -> flip routing FF -> revert commit if needed -> restart canary pods -> promote hotfix. Include commands and PR template.

mike: great response team — closing thread for operational chatter.
